newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bollore rises on capital change report.
newsitem.headline: Bollore rises on capital change report.

text.p: Shares in French holding company Bollore Technologies were among the biggest gainers on Monday, following a newspaper report which revived speculation about a shake-up in the group's capital, market sources said.
Weekly newspaper Le Journal des Finances reported at the weekend that the group was "ready to merge Albatross (Investissement) and Bollore, doubtless in the next few months".
Bollore stock was up 4.11 percent at 734 francs on a volume of 17,067 shares at 1414 GMT. Bollore has interests in tobacco, shipping, energy and production of film and speciality paper.
Albatross Investissement, the company which holds the Bollore family's shares in Bollore Technologies, has around 55 percent of the capital in the quoted company, a source close to Bollore said.

A fund manager said: "According to the press, there is talk of reducing the cascade (of holding companies in the group), which is always welcomed by the Bourse, which likes direct lines between shareholders and quoted companies."
However, the source said nothing was planned between Albatross and Bollore in the coming months.
Bollore Technologies told analysts last Friday the company could post an annual pre-tax pre-exceptional profit of around one billion francs by the end of the decade, the source said.

Bollore posted a 1996 first-half, pre-tax pre-exceptional profit of 337 million and if it doubled that for the full year it would make 700 million, and it could take that up to one billion by 2000, he said.
Albatross, quite separately from its 55 percent stake in Bollore Technologies, holds a 55 percent holding in Cie des Glenans, which in turn owns stakes in the Rivaud companies.

The cluster of companies loosely called the Rivaud group includes the troubled Banque Rivaud investment bank and Air Liberte, the private airline bought by British Airways Plc after the French firm crashed into insolvency last year.

The source confirmed the three main shareholders in the Rivaud constellation of companies have agreed to abolish double voting rights in Rivaud firms. The three shareholders are Edouard de Ribes, Hubert Fabri and Vincent Bollore.

But strictly speaking, the loss of double voting rights should have no direct effect on Bollore Technologies or the Rivaud companies as the main shareholders in the Rivaud group already hold majorities in each of the Rivaud companies, the source said.
Market operators have previously pointed to the lack of transparency in the structure of Bollore Technologies.
